question.text: The compound that does NOT liberate CO<sub>2</sub>, on treatment with aqueous sodium bicarbonate solution, is

solution.text: Except phenol, all other options are either carboxylic acids or sulphonic acids, which are comparatively strong. Phenol is a very weak acid <math> <mrow> <msub> <mtext>K</mtext> <mtext>a</mtext> </msub> <mo>≈</mo> <mn>1</mn> <msup> <mn>0</mn> <mrow> <mn>-1</mn> <mn>0</mn> </mrow> </msup> </mrow> </math> and  hence will not displace CO<sub>2</sub> from NaHCO<sub>3</sub>
